name: Water
everyday: Drinking water, rain, rivers and oceans.
explanation: Water contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
fact: About 60% of your body is water!

name: Oxygen Gas
everyday: The oxygen in the air you breathe.
explanation: Oxygen gas is made of molecules containing two oxygen atoms. Because it has only ONE kind of atom, it is still an element, not a compound.
fact: Oxygen gas makes up about 21% of the air.

name: Hydrogen Gas
everyday: A clean-burning fuel used in some buses and rockets.
explanation: Hydrogen gas is made of molecules containing two hydrogen atoms. One kind of atom means it is an element.
fact: Hydrogen gas is about 14 times lighter than air.

name: Nitrogen Gas
everyday: Most of the air around you.
explanation: Nitrogen gas molecules contain two nitrogen atoms. One kind of atom means it is an element.
fact: Liquid nitrogen is so cold (−196 °C) that it is used to freeze foods quickly.

name: Carbon Dioxide
everyday: The bubbles in soda; the gas you breathe out.
explanation: Carbon dioxide contains one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms. The small 2 is a subscript: it tells us there are two oxygen atoms.
fact: Plants take in carbon dioxide to make their food.

name: Carbon Monoxide
everyday: Detected by the CO alarms in many homes.
explanation: Carbon monoxide has one carbon atom and only ONE oxygen atom. A different ratio of atoms makes a completely different substance from CO₂ — one that is poisonous to breathe.
fact: "Mono" means one and "di" means two — that is how CO and CO₂ get their names.

name: Ozone
everyday: The ozone layer high in the sky blocks harmful UV light.
explanation: Ozone molecules contain three oxygen atoms. O₂ and O₃ are both forms of the element oxygen, but they behave differently.
fact: The ozone layer is 15–35 km above the ground.

name: Hydrogen Peroxide
everyday: A diluted form is used to clean cuts.
explanation: Hydrogen peroxide has two hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms. It uses the same elements as water, but a different ratio makes a different substance.
fact: It is sold in brown bottles because light breaks it down.

name: Sodium Chloride
everyday: Table salt on food; road salt for icy streets.
explanation: Table salt is an ionic compound made of sodium and chloride ions in a 1:1 ratio. It forms a crystal, not separate molecules, so NaCl describes one formula unit.
fact: Salt crystals are tiny cubes — just like blocks!

name: Calcium Carbonate
everyday: Chalk, limestone, marble, seashells and eggshells.
explanation: Calcium carbonate contains calcium, carbon and oxygen. Oxygen appears three times in one formula unit, shown by the subscript 3.
fact: The White Cliffs of Dover are made of chalk from tiny ancient sea creatures.

name: Methane
everyday: Natural gas used in many stoves and furnaces.
explanation: Methane contains one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms.
fact: Natural gas has no smell — companies add a smelly chemical so leaks can be noticed.

name: Ammonia
everyday: Used to make fertilizers that help crops grow.
explanation: Ammonia contains one nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms.
fact: Fertilizers made from ammonia help grow food for billions of people.

name: Iron(III) Oxide
everyday: Rust on old bikes, nails and cars.
explanation: Iron(III) oxide is an ionic compound with iron and oxide ions in a 2:3 ratio: 2 iron and 3 oxygen in each formula unit.
fact: Mars looks red because its dust contains iron oxide.

name: Sodium Bicarbonate
everyday: Baking soda, which helps cakes and cookies rise.
explanation: Baking soda contains sodium, hydrogen, carbon and oxygen: 1 Na, 1 H, 1 C and 3 O in each formula unit.
fact: Baking soda releases carbon dioxide bubbles that make dough fluffy.

name: Glucose
everyday: A sugar that living things use for energy.
explanation: Glucose contains 6 carbon, 12 hydrogen and 6 oxygen atoms — 24 atoms in all! Stack atoms in the crafting slots to fit them.
fact: Plants make glucose from carbon dioxide and water using sunlight.
